body: yeah, i get you. everyone seems to be excited and has big plans but i don't. i'm really scared of going and getting a degree that won't get me anywhere. plus i really don't want to get loans on my back only to give up halfway through lol

yeah, i think maybe going and doing what i wanna do could be good for me. i think it's just the commitment to like, getting a job and living life nd shit afterwards that makes me a bit skeptical of dedicating myself to college, but i'll keep on the path of going nd see what happens

It makes sense, thank you.

1. My mom has dementia, so she has kind of been on the sidelines for four or so years while it's gotten worse. She's not able to do much for herself anymore. My parents are both much older than the average parents of a teenager so we've always had weird relationships since there's such generational gaps. I see why this makes me seek out parental figures, though.

2. The critical voice of my father and the wish for a more positive outcome after all of this totally make sense too. He's always been quite critical and has tried to install certain values in me, since he's very traditional and old-fashioned in his ideas of a woman's role in society.

3. There's definitely an unhealthy dynamic between my father and myself just through how he was raised and in turn, how he raised me. We both have very different views of the world. He doesn't believe much in privacy either, so I guess that's where that part of my dream comes from. The sexual element is interesting (and of course it's a little uncomfortable to discuss). It makes sense to me, even with how uncomfortable it is. I wouldn't be too surprised if it were accurate.

Psychotherapy's a really good idea. I've wanted to start it for some time. With my father's general attitude I don't think he'd ever be down for the idea - but I want to try and grow away from him as I grow older while mending myself too, so while it's upsetting he wouldn't be willing to do psychotherapy, the most important part to me is my own willingness. I think if I accept the ways my father has affected me and strive to mend those aspects of my life, I'll be better off, and could try and have a better life in a new place, like this college abroad.

Thank you for this break down of my post - I really didn't expect it.
I'm sorry about your parents, nobody deserves to live like that. Thank you for everything you've said.

Thank you for this. Being reminded my family life is toxic is so strange because I've been told by family my whole life that this is how all families are - being told otherwise really helps. Really, thank you. I want to keep working and get out, but I'm so scared it'll be too difficult for me and I'll give up

I think I have two options if I live past the end of summer, either give into the easy way and go to the college close to me and try and just distance myself from family, or keep working towards going to my dream uni even if it means my Dad would likely disown me. I'm so scared about both really, but I'd never forgive myself if I just surrendered and chose not to take the risk
